title: observation: after `switchOrganization`, `user.positions` is still the PREVIOUS org's answer unless the server happens to rotate the session token
body:
Noticed while implementing #5619 (the unresolved-admin window) and deliberately left out of that PR — it is a different direction of the same leg, and unlike #5619 I could not close the last step of it from this repo.

## What is certain

framework `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` computes `user.positions[]` inside `customSession`, and its organization leg is keyed on the session:

```js
const orgId = (session as any)?.activeOrganizationId;
if (!orgId) return [];
```

So `positions` carries `org_owner` / `org_admin` / `org_member` **for whichever organization was active when the session payload was built**.

`AuthProvider.switchOrganization` (`packages/auth/src/AuthProvider.tsx`) does not rebuild that payload:

```ts
const org = await client.setActiveOrganization(orgId);
setActiveOrganization(org);
// … ActiveOrganizationStorage.set(org.id)
```

No `loadSession()`. The active-member row does re-resolve (the effect keyed on `activeOrganization`), so leg 1 catches up — but leg 3 keeps answering from the old organization.

`useWorkspaceAdminStatus` (post-#5619) is `leg1 || leg2 || leg3`, so a stale `org_owner` in `positions` reads as **admin** regardless of what the new organization's member row says. That is the over-permissive direction, which #5619's window is not: an owner of org A who switches into org B, where they are an ordinary member, can keep the admin affordances.

## What I could NOT determine, and why this is filed as an observation

There is a plausible path that already closes it. `createAuthClient` gives better-auth's client `customFetchImpl: bearerFetch`, and `bearerFetch` captures `set-auth-token` into `TokenStorage`; `TokenStorage.subscribeRotation` then drives `loadSession()` (objectui#4467). **If** the server re-issues a bearer token on `POST /organization/set-active`, identity re-resolves on its own and there is no defect here at all.

Whether it does is a framework/better-auth question that cannot be answered from this repo, and I did not have a live multi-org server to measure it against. Deciding it needs one measurement:

1. Sign in as an owner of org A who is an ordinary member of org B.
2. Switch to org B in the console.
3. Read `GET /api/v1/auth/get-session` and check whether `user.positions` still contains `org_owner`.

If it does, this is a real defect and the fix is presumably an explicit `refreshSession()` in `switchOrganization` — with the caveat that `refreshSession` deliberately does not raise `isLoading`, so the console would not blank during the switch.

## Not claimed

That server-side authorization is affected — it is not; the server re-derives from the session on every request. This is a client-side gating artefact only, the same class as #5619.

## Refs

- #5619 — the same leg, the other direction (unresolved rather than stale); its PR added `isMembershipResolved`, which already reports "unresolved" across a switch for **leg 1**, but cannot speak for leg 3.
- objectui#4467 — the rotation subscription that may or may not already cover this.
